title: Policy 2023-05 and 247 CMR 9.19(1)(f): stocking family planning medications and filling valid prescriptions for them
subtopic: Supply of family planning medications and timely access under Board Policy 2023-05
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.19(1)(f) a pharmacy shall maintain on the pharmacy premises the equipment, supplies, and medications necessary to conduct the practice of pharmacy in accordance with the usual needs of the community and scope of practice of the pharmacy. Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2023-05, Access to Reproductive Health Medications (effective date 3/22/23), states that the Department of Public Health, the Bureau of Health Professions Licensure and the Board want to be clear that all family planning medications, including mifepristone (Mifeprex), misoprostol (Cytotec), emergency contraception, and contraceptive prescriptions, are considered necessary to meet the usual needs of each and every community across the Commonwealth; that therefore all pharmacies located in Massachusetts and licensed by the Board must maintain a continuous, sufficient supply of all family planning medications, including those named, to meet the needs of the community; that in the event that any family planning medication is not immediately available for dispensing pursuant to a valid prescription and/or order, it is the responsibility of the licensed pharmacy and/or licensed pharmacist to ensure access to such family planning medication by the patient in a timely manner either by refilling the pharmacy's stock supply, contacting the prescriber for a reasonable alternative medication, transferring the prescription to another pharmacy where such medication is readily available for dispensing, or some other manner (i.e., mail order, central fill, etc.); and that any licensed pharmacy and/or pharmacist that refuses to stock, dispense, and/or fill any valid prescription and/or order for family planning medications, or impedes access in any way to any such medications, will be in violation of 247 CMR 9.19(1)(f) and practice standards, and any such violations will be investigated fully by the Board.
exam_relevance: Tests that the Board treats family planning medications, including emergency contraception and contraceptive prescriptions, as necessary to meet the usual needs of every community under 247 CMR 9.19(1)(f), the ways a pharmacy or pharmacist ensures timely access when such a medication is not immediately available, and the Board's statement that refusing to stock, dispense or fill a valid prescription or order for family planning medications violates 247 CMR 9.19(1)(f) and practice standards.

authority.name: Policy 2023-05: Access to Reproductive Health Medications
Pharmacy operation: equipment, supplies and medications for the usual needs of the community

common_confusions: Treating a family planning medication that is out of stock as ending the pharmacy's responsibility; the policy makes the licensed pharmacy and/or licensed pharmacist responsible for ensuring timely access, such as by refilling stock, contacting the prescriber for a reasonable alternative medication, transferring the prescription to another pharmacy where it is readily available, or another manner such as mail order or central fill.

Carrying the referral instruction for expedited partner therapy prescriptions in Policy 2020-08 over to a valid prescription or order for a family planning medication; Policy 2023-05 states that refusing to stock, dispense or fill such a prescription or order, or impeding access, violates 247 CMR 9.19(1)(f) and practice standards.

Reading the statement in Circular Letter DCP 26-08-125 that there is no requirement to prescribe contraceptives as reaching the filling of a valid contraceptive prescription written by another prescriber.
verification_notes: Read the full two-page text of Board Policy 2023-05 (effective date 3/22/23), linked as '2023-05: Access to Reproductive Health Medications' from the Policies and Circular Letters list on the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's Pharmacy Practice Resources page on mass.gov, and 247 CMR 9.19(1), including (f), with the exclusions in 247 CMR 9.19(23) and (24), in the current 247 CMR 9.00 publication on mass.gov (pages dated 12/6/24), on 2026-09-16.
